chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi al-Qurashi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Said ibn Ghazwan, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Satan does not cease to be fearful and panicked before the son of Adam as long as he prays the five prayers at their appointed times. But when he neglects them, Satan emboldens against him and leads him into great sins.

key_terms.الشيطان: Satan, the devil — the entity that tempts humans to sin
key_terms.الصلوات الخمس: The five daily prayers (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Satan's fear of those who pray on time?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (S) taught that performing the five daily prayers at their prescribed times serves as a shield against Satan's influence. This hadith, narrated through a chain reaching Imam Ali (AS), was originally delivered to the early Muslim community to emphasize the protective power of punctual prayer. In its original context, 'al-azaim' (great sins) referred to the major transgressions well-known to the early Muslim community, and the metaphor of Satan being 'in panic' conveyed that consistent worship creates a spiritual barrier evil cannot penetrate.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad b. `Ali al-Kufi al-Qurashi from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Faddal from Sa`id b. Ghazwan from Isma`il b. Abi Ziyad from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as) from Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (sw) said:
Satan does not stop pacing in panic from a child of Adam who prays the five prayers in accordance with their timings. When he loses them, he emboldens and leads him into great sins.
